# Concrete cap-pattern restrictions and a conditional Laplacian extraction

These lemmas identify additional structure needed beyond an abstract PSD
covariance stress. They do not prove the local 1/(2h(P)) bound.

## 1. Actual margin vectors respect the active Jensen relations

At a normal angle where the support functions are differentiable, a zero
Jensen gap g_a>=0 has g_a'=0. Thus the support-point array

    X_z=h_z n+h_z' t

satisfies every active relation sum_z q_az X_z=0. Constants and original
base coordinates also satisfy those relations. Consequently each actual
ambient cap has a margin vector

    f_j(z)=u_j.X_z+v_j.z-b_j

in the full active Jensen kernel. Its strict cap-membership indicator is
1_{f_j(z)>0}. At diffuse-almost-everywhere angles, any problematic boundary
coincidences have already been removed by the global stress theorem.

For any active anchored representation z=sum_w p_w w, a positive margin
at z forces a positive margin at some source. Hence the weighted coverage
q_z=sum_j lambda_j I_jz satisfies

    q_z <= sum_(w in support(p)) q_w.

These are actual sign traces of kernel vectors, rather than arbitrary
subsets of the fiber indices. They alone are not asserted sufficient for
a numerical depth bound. On a partial-curvature source pattern, the margin
vectors belong to the FULL active kernel; they need not vanish outside the
source pattern, so must not automatically be used as tests in L(theta).

## 2. Smooth cap-crossing cancellation

Assume on the full angular circle every fiber has a continuous strictly
positive curvature radius r_z. The common diffuse stress gives

    sum_z W_z(theta) r_z(theta)^2=0

almost everywhere. There are only finitely many crossing normals for each
fixed cap line: a strictly convex C2 positive-curvature boundary meets a
proper line in at most two points. Between the finitely many crossing
normals the indicators, and hence W, are constant. Continuity extends the
identity to both one-sided limits at each crossing angle theta_0. Therefore

    sum_(j,z) lambda_j Delta I_jz r_z(theta_0)^2=0.         (1)

For one fixed cap j, its transverse crossing signs at this angle are all
identical, since

    d f_j(z)/dtheta = r_z(theta) u_j.t(theta).

Thus a positive-weight cap cannot have an isolated crossing angle; another
cap must contribute an opposite tangential sign at that same angle.
Supporting tangencies do not change an indicator and are excluded from this
crossing assertion. Arbitrary diffuse curvature measures need not admit
pointwise continuous radii, so (1) is not claimed in that generality.

## 3. A genuine positive-variance decomposition under extra hypotheses

Suppose an active Jensen space is parametrized by freely prescribed
coordinates a_i on a set of k boundary indices:

    v=H a,

where H has nonnegative entries, each boundary row is the corresponding
standard basis vector, and all other rows are nonnegative interpolation
rows. Suppose W_z<=0 at every nonboundary index. Put

    Q=H^T diag(W) H.

Then Q_ij<=0 for i!=j, because boundary rows contribute no off-diagonal
terms, and every nonboundary contribution is nonpositive.

Assume Q is PSD and has a strictly positive null vector t. The matrix

    L=diag(t) Q diag(t)

is symmetric, has nonpositive off-diagonal entries, and has zero row sums.
Writing c_ij=-L_ij>=0 for i<j gives the exact identity

    a^T L a=sum_(i<j) c_ij(a_i-a_j)^2.                   (2)

Thus its nullspace consists of vectors constant on the connected components
of the graph with edges c_ij>0. If a family of positive curvature vectors is
H t(theta) and is annihilated by this same Q, then t_i(theta)/t_i is constant
within each such graph component. Each component therefore contributes one
common scalar curvature function with fixed positive fiber coefficients.
This is an actual homothetic-component mechanism.

The interpolation/sign hypotheses are essential. PSD plus positive null
curvature alone does not provide them; see
`candidate d056b64d0007e48a`. In that counterexample,
positive weights at dependent rows can make off-diagonal entries positive.
No cap-budget theorem is claimed without a further geometric argument
establishing the needed signs and free interpolation structure.
